title: Trace-polynomial map between q- and p-degree Artin–Schreier covers
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $q=p^r$ with $r\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with prime subfield $\mathbf F_p$ and field trace $\operatorname{Tr}=\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}:k_0\to\mathbf F_p$ (as in [def-fd-additive-character]), and let $b\in k_0^\times$. Let $X$ be a separated $k_0$-scheme of finite type [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Put $\pi_q:Y_q=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)\to X$ and $\pi_{p,b}:Y_{p,b}=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[t]/(t^p-t-bf)\to X$, and let $\sigma_c$ ($c\in k_0$) be the $X$-automorphism of $Y_q$ given by $y\mapsto y+c$ and $\tau_d$ ($d\in\mathbf F_p$) the $X$-automorphism of $Y_{p,b}$ given by $t\mapsto t+d$. Then:

1. $\pi_q$ is finite étale, and on the geometric fibre of $Y_q$ over every geometric point of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] the group $(k_0,+)$ acts simply transitively through $c\mapsto\sigma_c$; in particular every geometric fibre has $q$ points.
2. The additive polynomial $\Theta_b(y)=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(by)^{p^i}$ satisfies $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=b(y^q-y)$ in $\mathcal O_X[y]$, hence $\Theta_b(y)^p-\Theta_b(y)=bf$ in $\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)$, so $t\mapsto\Theta_b(y)$ defines an $X$-morphism $\theta_b:Y_q\to Y_{p,b}$.
3. $\theta_b\circ\sigma_c=\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}\circ\theta_b$ for every $c\in k_0$.
4. On the geometric fibres over every geometric point of $X$, $\theta_b$ is surjective, and each of its fibres is an orbit, under the $\sigma_c$, of the subgroup $\ker(c\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(bc))$ of order $q/p$.
5. For every morphism $h:X'\to X$ of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with $f'=h^*f$ and $Y'_q$, $Y'_{p,b}$, $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$, $\theta'_b$ formed from $(X',f')$ in the same way, the canonical isomorphisms $Y'_q\cong Y_q\times_XX'$ and $Y'_{p,b}\cong Y_{p,b}\times_XX'$ carry $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$ and $\theta'_b$ to the base changes of $\sigma_c$, $\tau_d$ and $\theta_b$.

proof.text: Use the already proved upstream AffineSpace.isFinite_artinSchreierMap and AffineSpace.etale_artinSchreierMap and stability under pullback. The cardinality q of a field is greater than one, and q=p^r vanishes on X because r is positive. This proves finiteness and etaleness of the actual pullback cover without relative-Spec algebra sheaves.

proof.text: The pullback universal property represents maps into a cover by a map to X and a global section y satisfying y^n-y=f. Equality of maps follows from equality over X and on y, using AffineSpace.hom_ext. Construct translations by the explicit section y+c; Frobenius additivity and c^q=c prove the equation, composition, and the inverse translation by -c. This works on the zero ring too.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: Lang torsor pushout; explicit polynomial calculation.

proof.text: Over an algebraically closed field, the equation y^q-y=a has a root since it is a polynomial of positive degree. Two roots have difference d satisfying d^q=d. Evaluate the factorization X^q-X=product over c in k of (X-c) using FiniteField.prod_sub_eq_zero_of_pow_card_eq: in a domain one factor is zero, so the roots differ by a unique k-constant. A finite geometric fibre is locally Artinian, so each of its points is closed. Mathlib pointOfClosedPoint supplies its rational section, and ext_of_apply_closedPoint_eq makes that section unique. The cover universal property shows its root coordinate determines the point. Therefore translations act simply transitively on each geometric fibre; the orbit bijection with k proves cardinality q.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: Lang torsor pushout; explicit polynomial calculation.

proof.text: The ring homomorphism iterateFrobeniusOfPrime is additive even for a zero ring when p vanishes. Induction on r telescopes the sum to obtain Theta_b^p-Theta_b=b(X^q-X), using b^q=b. Applying the quotient map gives bf. Evaluating this identity at the tautological root constructs theta by the same cover universal property; its root formula is definitionally the displayed trace polynomial.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: Lang torsor pushout; explicit polynomial calculation.

proof.text: Module.card_eq_pow_finrank and q=p^r imply finrank over ZMod p is r. FiniteField.algebraMap_trace_eq_sum_pow then identifies the sum of Frobenius powers of bc with Tr(bc). Apply Frobenius additivity to Theta_b(y+c) and compare the base map and root of the two composites to prove equivariance.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: Lang torsor pushout; explicit polynomial calculation.

proof.text: Algebra.trace_surjective for finite separable fields makes the trace onto ZMod p. Multiplication by nonzero b is a bijection with inverse multiplication by b inverse, so T(c)=Tr(bc) is onto too. The additive subgroup index of its kernel is the cardinality p of its range. The identity card(kernel) times index=card(k) yields card(kernel)=q/p.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: Lang torsor pushout; explicit polynomial calculation.

proof.text: Apply the simply transitive result to both covers. If z is in the q-cover then every target point is a unique translate of theta(z) by some d in ZMod p. Surjectivity of T and equivariance lift it by a translation of z. Two source points differ by a unique translation c; their images agree if and only if T(c)=0, since the prime-field action is free. This proves geometric surjectivity and the kernel-orbit clause.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: Lang torsor pushout; explicit polynomial calculation.

proof.text: For arbitrary h:Xprime to X, construct the comparison cover map by the tautological root and projection composed with h. Prove its square cartesian directly: any compatible pair of maps admits the unique lift prescribed by its coordinate. Pullback of k-constants along a k-morphism preserves them. Comparing projection and root now proves that both translations and the trace map commute with these comparisons. Map preservation of finite sums, products, and powers proves trace-polynomial naturality without flatness.
